notes:
1. Welfare-Oriented Schemes — Meaning

  • Welfare-oriented schemes are public programmes intended to reduce deprivation, expand access to essential services and strengthen social and economic capabilities.
  • They may address food, education, health, housing, employment, agriculture and social protection.
📌 Must-Memorise

Welfare Scheme → Protection + Capability + Inclusion

2. Welfare Is Broader Than Cash Assistance

Government welfare can be delivered through:

  • Cash.
  • Goods.
  • Services.
  • Insurance.
  • Assets.
  • Social protection.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Welfare ≠ Cash Transfer Alone

3. Protective Welfare

Protective welfare prevents households from falling into severe hardship.

Examples include:

  • Food security.
  • Social pensions.
  • Health financial protection.
📌 Must-Memorise

Protective Welfare → Prevents Deprivation

4. Promotional Welfare

Promotional welfare increases future capabilities.

Examples include:

  • Education.
  • Skills.
  • Agricultural productivity support.
  • Livelihood assistance.
📌 Must-Memorise

Promotional Welfare → Builds Productive Capacity

5. Transformative Welfare

Transformative welfare seeks to address deeper social inequalities.

Examples include:

  • Women's empowerment.
  • Disability inclusion.
  • Support for historically disadvantaged communities.

6. Welfare-State Constitutional Basis

The Preamble promises:

  • Social justice.
  • Economic justice.
  • Political justice.
  • Equality of status and opportunity.

These provide the broad philosophical foundation of welfare-oriented government.

7. Article 38

  • Article 38 directs the State to promote a social order based on justice and minimise inequalities.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 38 → Social Order + Reduction of Inequality

8. Article 39

Article 39 includes principles relating to:

  • Adequate livelihood.
  • Distribution of resources for common good.
  • Prevention of concentration of wealth.
  • Equal pay.
  • Protection of workers and children.

9. Article 41

  • Article 41 refers to public assistance in circumstances such as:
  • Unemployment.
  • Old age.
  • Sickness.
  • Disablement.
  • These responsibilities operate within the State's economic capacity.

10. Articles 42, 46 and 47

  • Article 42 → Humane working conditions + maternity relief.
  • Article 46 → Educational and economic advancement of weaker sections, especially SCs/STs.
  • Article 47 → Nutrition + standard of living + public health.
📌 Must-Memorise

Directive Principles → Constitutional Foundation of Welfare State

11. Tamil Nadu Welfare Architecture

Tamil Nadu's welfare system is distributed across multiple departments rather than concentrated in one ministry.

Important departments include:

  • Social Welfare and Women Empowerment.
  • School and Higher Education.
  • Health and Family Welfare.
  • Revenue and Disaster Management.
  • Rural Development.
  • Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
  • Labour.
  • Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare.
  • BC/MBC and Minorities Welfare.

12. Welfare Administration Chain

The basic administrative relationship is:

Beneficiary Need

→ Specialised Department

→ Scheme

→ Delivery Agency

→ Citizen

📌 Must-Memorise

Welfare Administration → Interdepartmental by Nature

13. Multiple Benefits to One Household

A single student may receive:

  • Nutrition.
  • Scholarship.
  • Transport support.
  • Higher-education assistance.

Therefore, one beneficiary may interact with several departments.

14. Universal Public Distribution System

Tamil Nadu operates a Universal Public Distribution System — UPDS.

  • The supplied source states that Tamil Nadu has followed the universal approach for more than 50 years.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tamil Nadu PDS → Universal Orientation

15. PDS Commodities

Under the applicable system, commodities can include:

  • Rice.
  • Wheat.
  • Sugar.
  • Kerosene.

The Special PDS also covers items such as:

  • Tur dal.
  • Palmolein oil.

16. Tamil Nadu PDS vs NFSA

  • NFSA provides nationally defined entitlements for specified categories.
  • Tamil Nadu's UPDS maintains broader State-level food-distribution coverage.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

NFSA Entitlement ≠ Entire Tamil Nadu PDS

17. Thayumanavar Scheme

  • The supplied source describes the Thayumanavar Scheme as providing home delivery of PDS commodities to eligible:
  • Persons aged above 65 years.
  • Persons with disabilities.
📌 Must-Memorise

Thayumanavar → PDS Last-Mile Home Delivery

18. Accessibility-Based Welfare

The Thayumanavar model represents the shift:

Benefit Available at Shop

→ Benefit Accessible to Mobility-Constrained Beneficiary

19. MGR Nutritious Meal Programme

  • Tamil Nadu's major Nutritious Meal Programme was introduced in 1982.
  • Its objectives include improving:
  • Nutrition.
  • Enrolment.
  • Attendance.
📌 Must-Memorise

MGR Nutritious Meal Programme → 1982

20. Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme

  • Announced in 2022.
  • Launched on 15 September 2022 at Madurai.
  • It provides breakfast to eligible primary-school children under the government-school framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

Breakfast Scheme → 15 September 2022 → Madurai

21. Nutrition Schemes — Welfare Type

School meals are primarily:

In-Kind / Service Benefits

rather than direct cash transfers.

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

School Meal ≠ Cash Welfare

22. Pudhumai Penn

The Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme, popularly known as Pudhumai Penn:

  • Supports eligible girl students.
  • Provides ₹1,000 per month under the scheme framework.
  • Uses Direct Benefit Transfer.
📌 Must-Memorise

Pudhumai Penn → ₹1,000 per Month → Eligible Girl Students

23. Pudhumai Penn — Objective

Its major objectives include:

  • Higher-education continuation.
  • Dropout reduction.
  • Women's empowerment.
  • Future workforce participation.

24. Tamil Pudhalvan

  • Tamil Pudhalvan was launched on 9 August 2024.
  • It supports eligible male higher-education students under specified educational-background conditions.
  • The source states monthly assistance of ₹1,000.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tamil Pudhalvan → 9 August 2024 → ₹1,000 per Month

25. Tamil Pudhalvan — Beneficiaries

  • The source cites approximately 3.28 lakh beneficiaries on the current portal.
⚠️ TNPSC Current-Fact Rule

Beneficiary numbers can change and should always be dated.

26. Educational-Welfare Transition

Tamil Nadu's education welfare increasingly follows:

School Access

→ School Completion

→ Higher-Education Retention

📌 Must-Memorise

Educational Welfare → Retention + Mobility

27. Women's Welfare — Multiple Instruments

Tamil Nadu's women's welfare includes:

  • Higher-education support.
  • Free bus travel.
  • Marriage assistance.
  • Service homes.
  • Widow welfare.
  • Livelihood interventions.

28. Free Bus Travel

  • Tamil Nadu provides free travel to women and specified other eligible categories in applicable ordinary-fare government bus services.
  • The source records the programme as operating since 2021.
📌 Must-Memorise

Free Bus Travel → Service Subsidy

29. Mobility as Welfare

Free transport support primarily reduces:

  • Travel expenditure.
  • Mobility barriers.
  • Cost of accessing work, education and services.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Free Bus Travel ≠ Cash Transfer

30. Marriage-Assistance Schemes

The source states that Tamil Nadu's Social Welfare Department lists five marriage-assistance schemes covering categories such as:

  • Poor parents' daughters.
  • Orphan girls.
  • Widow remarriage.
  • Daughters of widows.
  • Inter-caste married couples.

31. Girl Child Protection Scheme

Under the currently published framework cited in the source:

  • Scheme I → ₹50,000 deposit for an eligible family with one girl child.
  • Scheme II → ₹25,000 each where an eligible family has two girl children.
⚠️ Current-Fact Rule

Exact amounts must be checked against the latest scheme notification.

32. Cradle Baby Scheme

  • The Cradle Baby Scheme addresses:
  • Infant abandonment.
  • Female infanticide.
  • It provides a protective institutional mechanism for infants.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cradle Baby Scheme → Girl-Child Protection

33. Child-Welfare Continuum

Child welfare can be understood as:

Survival

→ Nutrition

→ Education

→ Protection

→ Future Opportunity

34. CMCHIS

CMCHIS stands for:

Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme

It provides financial protection for eligible hospital treatment through empanelled:

  • Government hospitals.
  • Private hospitals.

35. CMCHIS — Current Coverage

  • The supplied source states that the official portal currently reports around 1.48 crore families under the scheme and continuation of the present insurance arrangement through 2027.
⚠️ TNPSC Current-Fact Rule

Coverage numbers are dynamic administrative data.

36. Health Insurance as Welfare

The welfare pathway is:

Health Risk

→ Financial Protection

→ Access to Treatment

📌 Must-Memorise

CMCHIS → Insurance-Based Welfare

37. Insurance vs Public Health System

CMCHIS does not replace:

  • PHCs.
  • Government hospitals.
  • Preventive health services.
  • Community health programmes.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Health Insurance ≠ Entire Health Welfare System

38. Kalaignarin Kanavu Illam

  • Kalaignarin Kanavu Illam is a rural housing programme.
  • Its broad objective is moving towards a Hut-Free Tamil Nadu by 2030.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kalaignarin Kanavu Illam → Hut-Free Tamil Nadu by 2030

39. Housing Target

The source states that the original programme framework envisaged:

  • 8 lakh concrete houses.
  • Over six years.
  • First phase → one lakh houses during 2024–25.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

8 Lakh Houses → Programme Target

Not Completed Houses

40. Housing as Asset Welfare

Housing creates a durable household asset.

📌 Must-Memorise

Cash Benefit → Purchasing Power

Housing Benefit → Long-Term Asset

41. Social Security Pensions

Tamil Nadu's pension framework includes welfare for:

  • Senior citizens.
  • Widows.
  • Persons with disabilities.
  • Agricultural labourers.
  • Poor farmers.
  • Deserted wives.
  • Eligible destitute unmarried women.

42. Important Pension Categories

The source lists schemes such as:

  • Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension.
  • Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension.
  • Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension.
  • Destitute Widow Pension.
  • Differently Abled Pension.
  • Unmarried Women Pension.
  • Uzhavar Pathukappu Old Age Pension.

43. Social Pension vs Employee Pension

  • Social-security pension → Welfare-oriented minimum income support.
  • Government employee pension → Arises from employment/service framework.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Social Pension ≠ Retirement Pension of Government Employee

44. Farmer Welfare

Agricultural welfare can combine:

  • Production support.
  • Extension.
  • Technology.
  • Input assistance.
  • Income protection.
  • Seasonal packages.
📌 Must-Memorise

Farmer Welfare ≠ Cash Assistance Alone

45. Kuruvai Special Package — 2026

According to the supplied source:

  • Kuruvai Special Package — 2026 allocation → ₹134.83 crore.
  • It covered notified Delta and non-Delta districts under the applicable framework.
⚠️ TNPSC Current-Fact Rule

₹134.83 crore → 2026-specific allocation

46. Digital Farmer Services

Tamil Nadu's Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Department also uses:

  • Farmer registration.
  • Agrisnet.
  • Digital extension services.

These connect welfare with agricultural productivity support.

47. Welfare Boards for Workers

Tamil Nadu uses specialised Welfare Boards for sections of unorganised labour.

Typical benefits may include:

  • Education.
  • Marriage.
  • Maternity.
  • Accident.
  • Disability.
  • Death.
  • Old age.

48. Welfare-Board Model

The basic relationship is:

Worker Registration

→ Institutional Coverage

→ Welfare Eligibility

📌 Must-Memorise

Registration Is Often Essential for Welfare-Board Benefits

49. Vulnerable-Community Welfare

Specialised welfare systems exist for:

  • SCs.
  • STs.
  • BCs.
  • MBCs.
  • DNCs.
  • Minorities.
  • Persons with disabilities.
  • Transgender persons.

50. Why Targeted Welfare Exists

Different groups face different barriers.

Examples:

  • Disability → Accessibility barrier.
  • Tribal communities → Geographic/habitat barriers.
  • Historically oppressed castes → Social exclusion.
📌 Must-Memorise

Same Benefit for Everyone ≠ Equal Welfare Outcome

51. Rural Community-Based Welfare

Rural welfare includes:

  • Self-Help Groups.
  • Employment programmes.
  • Housing.
  • Sanitation.
  • Local infrastructure.

It extends beyond individual cash transfers.

52. Self-Help Groups

SHGs combine:

Savings

  • Credit
  • Collective Organisation
  • Livelihood
📌 Must-Memorise

SHG → Community-Based Economic Empowerment

53. Major Welfare Delivery Instruments

Government welfare can broadly take six forms:

  • Cash transfer.
  • In-kind transfer.
  • Service subsidy.
  • Insurance.
  • Asset creation.
  • Institutional service.

54. Examples by Welfare Instrument

  • Cash → Pudhumai Penn/Tamil Pudhalvan.
  • In-kind → PDS/school meals.
  • Service subsidy → Free bus travel.
  • Insurance → CMCHIS.
  • Asset creation → Housing.
  • Institutional service → Hostels/care homes.
📌 Must-Memorise

Delivery Instrument Must Match the Problem

55. DBT

DBT stands for:

Direct Benefit Transfer

Potential advantages include:

  • Better traceability.
  • Faster payment.
  • Reduced cash handling.
  • Improved monitoring.

56. Last-Mile Welfare Delivery

Effective welfare depends on:

  • Correct beneficiary identification.
  • Correct records.
  • Bank details where applicable.
  • Accessible application systems.
  • Assisted access.

The administrative objective is:

Right Beneficiary

  • Right Benefit
  • Right Time
  • Accessible Delivery

57. Convergence

Convergence means coordinating different schemes or departments around a beneficiary's or community's needs.

Example:

Nutrition

  • Education
  • Transport
  • Scholarship
  • Health

may all affect one student's development.

📌 Must-Memorise

Convergence → Beneficiary-Centred Governance

58. Fiscal Sustainability and Outcome Orientation

The supplied Economic Survey reports social-sector expenditure rising from about:

  • ₹1.13 lakh crore in 2021–22

to

  • ₹1.58 lakh crore in the 2025–26 Revised Estimate.

Welfare must be evaluated by outcomes such as:

  • Education retention.
  • Lower food insecurity.
  • Better health.
  • Housing security.
  • Reduced vulnerability.

The long-term principle is:

Adequate Welfare

  • Effective Delivery
  • Productive Investment
  • Fiscal Sustainability

59. TNPSC Traps

  • Welfare schemes are not limited to cash transfers.
  • Protective, promotional and transformative welfare perform different functions.
  • Article 38 relates to a social order based on justice and reduction of inequalities.
  • Article 39 includes livelihood, common-good resource distribution and equal-pay principles.
  • Article 41 includes public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.
  • Article 42 concerns humane working conditions and maternity relief.
  • Article 46 particularly concerns weaker sections, especially SCs and STs.
  • Article 47 concerns nutrition, standard of living and public health.
  • Tamil Nadu welfare administration is spread across many departments.
  • One citizen may receive benefits from several departments.
  • Tamil Nadu follows a Universal PDS orientation.
  • NFSA benefits and the entire Tamil Nadu PDS are not identical.
  • Thayumanavar Scheme is associated with last-mile PDS delivery to eligible elderly and disabled beneficiaries.
  • MGR Nutritious Meal Programme → 1982.
  • Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme → 15 September 2022, Madurai.
  • School meals are in-kind/service benefits, not cash transfers.
  • Pudhumai Penn full name → Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme.
  • Pudhumai Penn support in the supplied framework → ₹1,000 per month.
  • Tamil Pudhalvan launched → 9 August 2024.
  • Tamil Pudhalvan monthly assistance → ₹1,000 under the source framework.
  • Tamil Pudhalvan beneficiary count of 3.28 lakh is a current portal figure, not a permanent fact.
  • Free bus travel is a service subsidy, not a cash transfer.
  • The source lists five marriage-assistance schemes.
  • Girl Child Protection Scheme deposit amounts are current scheme parameters and can change.
  • Cradle Baby Scheme relates to child protection, not school nutrition.
  • CMCHIS is health insurance-based welfare.
  • CMCHIS is not the entire public-health system.
  • The source cites around 1.48 crore families under CMCHIS as current administrative data.
  • Kalaignarin Kanavu Illam aims at a Hut-Free Tamil Nadu by 2030.
  • Eight lakh houses is a programme target, not a completed achievement.
  • Housing welfare creates a durable asset.
  • Social-security pension and government employee pension are different.
  • Farmer welfare can include production support, technology and extension.
  • Kuruvai Special Package allocation of ₹134.83 crore is 2026-specific.
  • Welfare-board benefits often depend on registration.
  • Exact welfare-board benefit amounts vary by board and current rules.
  • Specialised welfare does not necessarily violate equality; it may address different barriers.
  • Same benefit to everyone does not always produce equal outcomes.
  • SHGs combine savings, credit and livelihood support.
  • PDS → In-kind transfer.
  • Pudhumai Penn → Cash/DBT.
  • Free bus travel → Service subsidy.
  • CMCHIS → Insurance.
  • Housing scheme → Asset creation.
  • DBT is a delivery mechanism, not a welfare scheme.
  • Digital application alone does not guarantee last-mile access.
  • Beneficiary identification errors can exclude eligible citizens.
  • Convergence means coordination across schemes/departments.
  • Convergence seeks beneficiary-centred rather than department-centred welfare.
  • Centre-sponsored and State-specific schemes can coexist in one delivery framework.
  • High welfare expenditure alone does not prove effectiveness.
  • Nutrition, education and health expenditure can improve human capital.
  • Welfare outcomes should be measured, not just allocations.
  • Fiscal sustainability remains necessary for long-term welfare.
  • The correct welfare principle is Protection + Capability + Inclusion + Sustainable Delivery.

60. Rapid Revision — TNPSC Most Expected

  • Welfare-oriented scheme means? → Public programme to reduce deprivation and improve capabilities.
  • Three broad welfare functions? → Protective, promotional and transformative.
  • Protective welfare does what? → Prevents severe hardship.
  • Promotional welfare does what? → Builds future capabilities.
  • Transformative welfare does what? → Addresses deeper social disadvantage.
  • Welfare only means cash? → No.
  • Article 38? → Social order based on justice and reduction of inequalities.
  • Article 39? → Livelihood, resource distribution, equal pay and protection.
  • Article 41? → Public assistance in specified vulnerable conditions.
  • Article 42? → Humane work conditions and maternity relief.
  • Article 46? → Weaker sections, especially SC/ST educational and economic interests.
  • Article 47? → Nutrition, standard of living and public health.
  • Tamil Nadu welfare architecture concentrated in one department? → No.
  • Tamil Nadu PDS model? → Universal Public Distribution System.
  • UPDS full form? → Universal Public Distribution System.
  • Tamil Nadu UPDS has operated for roughly how long according to source? → More than 50 years.
  • Thayumanavar Scheme relates to? → Home delivery of PDS commodities to specified elderly/PwD beneficiaries.
  • MGR Nutritious Meal Programme year? → 1982.
  • Breakfast Scheme launched? → 15 September 2022.
  • Launch place? → Madurai.
  • Pudhumai Penn monthly assistance? → ₹1,000.
  • Pudhumai Penn mainly supports? → Eligible girl students in higher education.
  • Tamil Pudhalvan launch date? → 9 August 2024.
  • Tamil Pudhalvan monthly assistance? → ₹1,000.
  • Free bus travel welfare type? → Service subsidy.
  • Cradle Baby Scheme addresses? → Infant abandonment/female infanticide.
  • Girl Child Protection Scheme is primarily? → Girl-child welfare and protection.
  • CMCHIS full form? → Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme.
  • CMCHIS welfare type? → Insurance-based financial protection.
  • CMCHIS replaces PHCs? → No.
  • Kalaignarin Kanavu Illam relates to? → Rural housing.
  • Main goal? → Hut-Free Tamil Nadu by 2030.
  • Programme target mentioned? → 8 lakh concrete houses over six years.
  • Housing is what type of welfare? → Asset creation.
  • Social-security pension provides? → Minimum income support to vulnerable groups.
  • Social pension and employee pension same? → No.
  • Kuruvai Special Package 2026 allocation in source? → ₹134.83 crore.
  • Farmer welfare only means income assistance? → No.
  • Welfare Boards mainly support? → Registered workers, especially unorganised workers.
  • Worker welfare model? → Registration → Coverage → Eligibility.
  • Why targeted welfare? → Different groups face different disadvantages.
  • SHG full form? → Self-Help Group.
  • SHGs combine? → Savings + Credit + Collective Organisation + Livelihood.
  • Main welfare delivery types? → Cash, in-kind, service subsidy, insurance, assets and institutional services.
  • PDS is what type? → In-kind transfer.
  • Student monthly assistance? → Cash transfer/DBT.
  • CMCHIS? → Insurance.
  • Housing? → Asset creation.
  • DBT full form? → Direct Benefit Transfer.
  • DBT is a welfare scheme? → No, a delivery mechanism.
  • Last-mile objective? → Right beneficiary + Right benefit + Right time + Accessible delivery.
  • Convergence means? → Coordination of different schemes or departments.
  • Beneficiary-centred governance means? → Services organised around people's needs rather than departmental silos.
  • Social-sector expenditure 2025–26 RE in source? → About ₹1.58 lakh crore.
  • Welfare spending automatically unproductive? → No.
  • Good welfare evaluation should focus on? → Outcomes.
  • Long-term welfare principle? → Adequate Welfare + Effective Delivery + Productive Investment + Fiscal Sustainability.
  • Core chapter chain? → Need → Scheme → Delivery → Protection/Capability → Improved Welfare Outcome.
